skill.name: ticktick-cli
skill.description: Manage Dida365 and TickTick projects, tasks, focus records, and habits through a Python CLI that uses the Open API and local OAuth.
skill.summary: Use a Python CLI to manage TickTick or Dida365 data through the Open API.
skill.author: DCjanus

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, plain imports, loopback OAuth, and intended API traffic. The OAuth client name does disclose the local hostname to TickTick or Dida365. Semantic review also found unpinned runtime dependencies, delayed token permission hardening, unrestricted @path reads, and destructive commands without enforced confirmation.

remediation.issue: Runtime dependencies use open-ended minimum versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact reviewed versions and use a lock file or verified hashes for reproducible installation.

remediation.issue: The OAuth token is written before restrictive permissions apply.
remediation.suggestion: Create the file atomically with mode 0600, reject symbolic links, and replace the final path only after a successful write.

remediation.issue: The @path options can read any accessible JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict file reads to an approved directory and require explicit user confirmation with a payload preview before remote mutations.

remediation.issue: Delete commands execute without an application-level confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require an interactive prompt or explicit --yes flag for project, task, and focus deletion.

remediation.issue: The default OAuth client name includes the local hostname.
remediation.suggestion: Use a generic client name by default and make device identification an explicit user option.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Dependencies
semantic_findings.description: The uv script uses minimum dependency versions instead of exact versions or hashes. Running the CLI can install newer package code that was not reviewed with this skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The dependency block explicitly uses greater-than-or-equal constraints for four runtime packages and provides no lock file or hashes.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth Token Is Restricted After Writing
semantic_findings.description: The token file is written before chmod applies mode 0600. A newly created file can briefly inherit broader permissions, and the write also follows an existing symbolic link.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code calls write_text before chmod and does not use exclusive creation or a no-follow flag. The exposure depends on local permissions and timing.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Local JSON Files Can Feed Remote Mutations
semantic_findings.description: Several options accept @path, read any accessible JSON file, and use its contents in TickTick mutation payloads. An agent could expose sensitive structured data after a misleading request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parsers expand user-provided paths without directory restrictions, and the documentation recommends @path inputs for API payloads.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Commands Lack Enforced Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: Project, task, and focus deletion commands call the remote delete methods immediately. The documentation asks the agent to confirm some deletions, but the CLI does not enforce that safeguard.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each delete handler invokes the API without a prompt or confirmation flag. The only safeguard is prose directed at the calling agent.

content.user_title: Manage TickTick Tasks from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Manual TickTick updates slow scripted workflows and AI agents. This skill manages projects, tasks, focus records, and habits through a Python CLI and OAuth.
actual_capabilities: Authenticate Dida365 or TickTick accounts through a local OAuth PKCE callback.
List, retrieve, create, update, and delete projects.
Create, update, complete, delete, move, and filter tasks.
Manage task tags, reminders, dates, priorities, and checklist items.
Retrieve and delete focus records for selected time ranges.
List, create, update, and check in habits.
limitations: Requires uv, Python 3.14 or later, network access, and installable dependencies.
Requires an authorized TickTick or Dida365 account and a local token file.
Supports only operations exposed by the implemented Open API client.
Delete commands execute immediately after invocation and need prior user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Review Daily Work
use_cases.description: List active projects and filter incomplete tasks for a clear daily review.

use_cases.title: Automate Task Intake
use_cases.description: Create structured tasks with dates, reminders, tags, priorities, and checklists.

use_cases.title: Operate Through an AI Agent
use_cases.description: Let an agent query and update TickTick data with machine-readable command output.
use_cases.target_user: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code users

prompt_templates.title: List My Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: List my TickTick projects. Show each project name and identifier. Do not change any data.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task named [title] in project [project]. Set due date [date], priority [priority], and tags [tags].

prompt_templates.title: Review Open Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Find incomplete tasks in project [project] between [start] and [end]. Group them by priority and summarize overdue items.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Batch Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Review tasks matching [criteria]. Propose moves, updates, or completions. Show the plan first and wait for confirmation before changing remote data.

output_examples.input: List my projects without changing anything.
output_examples.output: Found four projects: Inbox, Work, Personal, and Learning. Each project includes its identifier and view mode.

output_examples.input: Create a high-priority report task due Friday with two checklist items.
output_examples.output: Created the report task in the selected project. It is high priority, due Friday, and contains the two requested checklist items.

output_examples.input: Show incomplete work tasks due this week.
output_examples.output: Found seven incomplete tasks due this week. Three are high priority, and one is already overdue.

best_practices: Use read-only list, get, or filter commands before planning remote changes.
Confirm project, task, or focus deletion with the user before execution.
Use machine-readable output for agent workflows and keep global options before subcommands.
anti_patterns: Do not run authentication diagnostics before every normal operation.
Do not place sensitive data in @path payload files without reviewing the destination.
Do not execute batch updates or deletions without showing the planned changes first.

faq.question: Which account regions are supported?
faq.answer: Dida365 is the default region. Select TickTick during login for an international account.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The CLI uses OAuth with PKCE and a temporary callback server bound to localhost.

faq.question: Where is the token stored?
faq.answer: The default path is the TickTick CLI directory under the user config folder. TICKTICK_TOKEN_FILE can override it.

faq.question: Can it create and update checklist items?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply repeated item titles or a structured checklist payload from text or a reviewed file.

faq.question: Does it support focus records and habits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can retrieve or delete focus records and manage habits and check-ins.

faq.question: Does it confirm destructive actions?
faq.answer: No. The calling agent or user must confirm intent before invoking a delete command.
